title: Roman calumny: Protestants deny inherent righteousness
source_text: I. Solenne est Doctoribus Ecclesiae Romanae in Protestantes invehi, quasi nullam in fidelibus internam & inhaerentem justitiam agnoscerent, nec concederent ullam interioris hominis per Spiritus gratiam renovationem & sanctificationem. Sic Bellarminus affirmat Calvinum cum Lutheranis nullam inhaerentem justitiam admittere, De Just. lib. 2. cap. 3. Becanus eidem Calvino tribuit hanc propositionem, In justificatione non infundi gratiam & justitiam, qua homo interius renovetur, & in se fiat justus & sanctus; sed tantum imputari illi externam justitiam Christi, qua extra se justus esse censeatur. Vt Inst. Calvini, cap. 2.
pass_a_gloss: It is customary for the doctors of the Roman Church to inveigh against the Protestants as if they acknowledged no internal and inherent righteousness in believers, and as if they conceded no renovation and sanctification of the inner man by the Spirit's grace. Thus Bellarmine affirms that Calvin with the Lutherans admits no inherent righteousness (De Justificatione, book 2, chapter 3). Becanus attributes to the same Calvin this proposition: that in justification grace and righteousness by which a man is inwardly renewed and made just and holy in himself are not infused, but only Christ's external righteousness is imputed to him, by which he is reckoned just outside himself—citing Calvin's Institutes, chapter 2.
pass_b_english: Roman doctors charge Protestants with denying all internal inherent righteousness and Spirit-wrought renovation.
Bellarmine and Becanus pin on Calvin: only Christ's external justice imputed, nothing infused.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1035.
